chunks.text: This paper presents a novel approach to efficient large language model training. We introduce gradient checkpointing techniques that reduce memory consumption by up to 40% while maintaining training stability.

Our method employs a hierarchical checkpointing strategy that selectively stores activations at different granularities. We implement a dynamic memory allocation algorithm that adapts to the available GPU memory.
The training pipeline consists of three main stages: forward pass with selective checkpointing, backward pass with recomputation, and gradient accumulation. We optimize each stage independently.
Experiments on GPT-2 and BERT models show 35-42% memory reduction with less than 5% training time overhead. The method scales effectively to models with up to 1B parameters.
We investigate the application of reinforcement learning to robotic manipulation tasks. Our approach combines imitation learning with policy gradient methods.
The training process uses a two-stage approach: first, we collect expert demonstrations using kinesthetic teaching. Second, we fine-tune the policy using PPO.
